nodes.name: Heterogeneous Nucleation Soaking
nodes.procedure: A seed-assisted heterogeneous nucleation (HN) soaking process was employed to synthesize the NiFe-LDH catalyst supported on the layered Ni meshes at 25°C for 24 hours, a procedure analogous to that used for CAPistL1 (a robust catalyst strengthened by a dense interlayer, where CAP stands for the Center for artificial photosynthesis) but utilizing a different substrate.
nodes.source_text: First, a seed-assisted heterogeneous nucleation (HN) soaking process was employed to synthesize the NiFe-LDH catalyst supported on the layered Ni meshes at 25°C, a procedure analogous to that used for CAPistL1 (a robust catalyst strengthened by a dense interlayer, where CAP stands for the Center for artificial photosynthesis, Figure S1) but utilizing a different substrate.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Selenization
nodes.procedure: A hydrothermal treatment was used to obtain the selenium-modified NiFeSe material from the NiFe-LDH catalyst. The hydrazine hydrate with strong reducibility plays a main role in decreasing the oxidation state of Ni and Fe cations in the materials, resulting in the reduction of Ni to Ni⁰ (metallic nickel) and Fe³⁺ to Fe²⁺ and even into Fe⁰ (metallic Fe). The XRD pattern shows typical peaks at around 32.7°-34.4° belonging to Fe₃Se₄. The Ni/Fe molecular ratio is 3.1/1 as determined by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). XPS analysis shows the appearance of Se⁻ and Se²⁻ peaks at binding energies of 55.0 and 53.8 eV, respectively, indicating that the NiFe-based catalyst has been selenicated.

unit_operations.name: Hydrothermal Selenization
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: A hydrothermal treatment was used to obtain the selenium-modified NiFeSe material

nodes.source_text: Second, a hydrothermal treatment was used to obtain the selenium-modified NiFeSe material. According to the scanning electron microscopy image, NiFeSe presents a highly interconnected network within the porous nanosheet structure, resembling coral-like formations. The Ni 2p peaks indicate the presence of Ni⁰ in NiFeSe, suggesting the reduction process of the hydrothermal treatment to obtain metallic nickel. Similar results can be found from Fe 2p of NiFeSe, in which Fe³⁺ is reduced into Fe²⁺ and even into Fe⁰ (metallic Fe) after the reductively hydrothermal process.

nodes.description: OER performance in 1.0 M KOH at 25°C in three-electrode system
nodes.source_text: The NiFeSe catalyst demonstrates a low overpotential of about 190 mV at 1000 mA cm⁻² outperforming the NiFe-LDH (222 mV at 1000 mA cm⁻²). With an overpotential of 234 mV, the NiFeSe exhibits a high current density of ~6000 mA cm⁻². The lower Tafel slope of NiFeSe (29.7 ± 2.2 mV dec⁻¹) compared to NiFe-LDH (31.8 ± 3.6 mV dec⁻¹) further evidences the faster OER kinetics of NiFeSe.

nodes.description: Bubble behavior analysis at 10 mA/cm² in 1.0 M KOH at 25°C
nodes.source_text: NiFeSe shows oxygen bubbles on the surface with a much smaller size than that of NiFe-LDH. NiFeSe delivers a narrower range of bubble size (i.e., 0-200 μm with an average size of 98.3 μm). The oxygen bubble takes ~3.15 s for NiFeSe to finish the lifecycle from formation to detachment. Adhesive force measurements were conducted in 1 M KOH to reveal a lower adhesion for NiFeSe (ΔF ≈ 0 μN).
